place_name: Camp Dennison, Ohio
source_note: ERM enlisted 18 June 1861 as a private, Co. A, 6th Ohio Infantry. The 6th Ohio was reorganized for three years' service at Camp Dennison, Ohio, on that date. Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html); ERM biography.

place_name: Fetterman, Va. (now Grafton, W. Va.)
source_note: "Moved to Fetterman, W. Va., June 29-July 2 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Grafton, Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: address to Com A 6th Reg at Grafton & it will follow the regiment.
source_note: "At Grafton, W. Va., July 2, 1861." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html). Quote: ERM to his parents, 10 July 1861, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Philippi, Va. (now W. Va.)
source_note: "March to Philippi July 4 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Laurel Hill, Va. (near Belington, now W. Va.)
quote: We heared a report Here yesterday which cast a gloom over our camp. it was that our reg had been in an Engagement & were all killed but 200 & the rest taken prisoners. This is a base lie.
source_note: "Laurel Hill July 8 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html). Quote: ERM to his parents, "Laurel Hill Va July 10" 1861, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Corrick's (Carrick's) Ford, Va. (near Parsons, now W. Va.)
source_note: "Carrick's Ford July 13 [1861]. Pursuit of Garnett's forces July 15-16." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Beverly, Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: It is very cold in these mountains at night. it is nothing strange to see frost here in the morning And the people here say they often have frost in evry month in the year.
source_note: "Duty at Beverly till August 6 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html). Quote: ERM to his mother, Beverly, Va., 17 Aug. 1861, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp Elkwater, foot of Cheat Mountain, Va. (now W. Va.)
source_note: "Camp at Elkwater, foot of Cheat Mountain, August 6-November 19 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Cheat Mountain Pass / Cheat Summit Fort, Va. (now W. Va.)
source_note: "Operations on Cheat Mountain against Lee September 11-17. Cheat Mountain Pass September 12 [1861]." Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Tygart Valley, Va. (now W. Va.) — reconnaissance
source_note: "Reconnoissance up Tygart Valley September 26-29 [1861]." Coordinates are a mid-valley approximation; the record does not fix the turning point. Source: Dyer's Compendium, 6th Regiment Ohio Infantry, 3 years (ohiocivilwar.com/cw6.html)

place_name: Columbus, Ohio (Ohio Adjutant General's Office)
quote: The Governor of Ohio has selected you for the purpose of enlisting in a company of volunteers for the US Service... you will repair forthwith to Columbus Ohio, where you will receive the appointment of Second Lieutenant
source_note: ERM commissioned 2nd Lieutenant, Co. F, 75th Ohio Infantry, 5 Oct. 1861. Adjutant General C. P. Buckingham had written him on 27 Sept. 1861 ordering him to Columbus. Quote: Buckingham to Monfort, 27 Sept. 1861, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp McLean, near Cincinnati (Wyoming), Ohio
source_note: "[75th Ohio] Organized at Camp McLean, Cincinnati, Ohio, November 7, 1861, to January 8, 1862." ERM recruited and drilled Co. F here. Start date is approximate (he was commissioned 5 Oct.). Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Glendale, Ohio (the Monfort family home)
quote: According to promise I send you a line this morning to inform of the time when I hope to have the pleasure of visiting Glendale.
source_note: The Rev. Joseph Glass Monfort's household was at Glendale, Hamilton Co., Ohio; ERM was home from Camp McLean during the regiment's organization. Quote: Mac Casterlin to E. R. Monfort, 1 Dec. 1861, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Cincinnati, Ohio — regiment embarks for western Virginia
quote: After we parted with you at Cincinnati we were very busy Assisting in loading the Camp Equipage & getting the men on board... I witnessed a great many very affecting scenes Soldiers parting with their friends & never expecting to See them again.
source_note: "Left State for Grafton, W. Va., January 28, 1862." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM to his sister Maggie, Parkersburg, 27 Jan. 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Parkersburg, Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: We remained at Parkersburgh two days & nights I never was so sick of a place in my life before.
source_note: ERM's letter of 27 Jan. 1862 is headed Parkersburg; his letter of 31 Jan. confirms a two-day stop. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Newburg, Va. (Preston Co., now W. Va.)
quote: Our camp is situate in a beautiful little meadow 13 miles from Grafton on the B. & O. R.R. at a deserted little town called Newburgh with about 10 or fifteen inhabitant
source_note: Quote and location: ERM to his sister, "Newburg. Jan 31st" [1862], Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp "Calvary Morris" (camp not identified; regiment then on the B. & O. between Grafton and Huttonsville, W. Va.)
quote: Guard duty is rather a severe way of serving your country though comes only once a week.
source_note: ERM's letter of 15 Feb. 1862 is headed "Camp Calvary Morris." The camp has not been identified in the regimental literature; coordinates shown are Grafton, the regiment's supply base, NOT a located camp site. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Laurel Mountain, W. Va. — march from Grafton to Huttonsville
quote: the Bloody Seventy Fifth might have been seen winding its way carelessly over the Laurel mountains wet to the skin from the rain which poured down incessantly from Eight in the morning till between 9 & ten then it began to freeze & hail
source_note: "March to Huttonville February 17-March 1, 1862." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote (describing 22 Feb. 1862): ERM to his sister, Camp Milroy, 5 March 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html). See also E. R. Monfort, "From Grafton to McDowell Through Tygart's Valley" (Ohio MOLLUS, 1886).

place_name: Camp Milroy, near Huttonsville, W. Va.
quote: I sent a wooden Bible which I carved cut of Laurel root I hope you received it safe as it is a curiosity that you may prize.
source_note: ERM's letters of 5 and 28 March 1862 are headed Camp Milroy; his letter of 26 April 1862 says "we left Camp Milroy on the sixth of April." Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html) and Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Cheat Mountain, W. Va. — on the march east
quote: We left our beautiful Camp near Huttonsville on sunday the Sixth of April. I was in command of the rear guard.
source_note: Quote: ERM to his sister, Monterey, 15 April 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html). Note: Dyer's records an "Expedition to Lost River Region April 1-12" for the regiment; ERM's own account places him on the Staunton-Parkersburg route toward Monterey, and his letter is preferred here.

place_name: Camp Allegheny (Alleghany Mountain), Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: We arose bright and early on Monday Morning started at 7oclock for the rebel camp camp on the Alleghania Mountains. Which was evacuated by them on the 5th
source_note: Quote: ERM to his sister, Monterey, 15 April 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Monterey, Highland County, Va.
quote: We have not seen the sun since we left Camp Milroy on the sixth of April. We have had either rain or snow all this time since & is quite an uncommon thing to have dry feet.
source_note: "Action at Monterey April 12 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM to his father, Camp at Monterey, 26 April 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp Constable, McDowell, Highland County, Va.
quote: I do not think there is much danger of the officers or men of the 75th Regt becoming dissipated in this country
source_note: ERM to his father, headed "Camp Constable Va / McDouel Highland co / May 2nd 1862" (catalogued 22 May 1862). Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp at Shaw's Fork, Shenandoah Mountain, Highland County, Va.
quote: We left Monterey on the 30th of April arriving at McDouel at 3oclock P.M. here we remained one day. on the morning of the 2nd of May we left McDouel for Shanandoah Mountain
source_note: ERM's letter is headed "Camp at Shaws Fork 6 1/2 miles from McDouel & 3 1/4 from Top of Shanandoah Mountain," 6 May 1862. Coordinates derived from that description along the Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike; not a surveyed site. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Battle of McDowell, Highland County, Va.
source_note: "Battle of McDowell May 8 [1862]." The 75th Ohio lost 87 men. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); Wikipedia, "75th Ohio Infantry Regiment." The McDowell battlefield lies inside the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District but is not a National Park Service unit.

place_name: Retreat to Franklin, Pendleton County, Va. (now W. Va.)
source_note: "Retreat to Franklin May 10-12 [1862]." Coordinates are a midpoint on the retreat road. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Franklin, Pendleton County, Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: I am very sorry to loose Lieut. Crampton. he was my only companion in trouble & in pleasure. I have just bid him good by
source_note: ERM's letters of 14 and 19 May 1862 are headed Franklin. Dyer's also lists an action at "Franklin May 29," but ERM wrote that the regiment "left Franklin on the 25th of May"; the discrepancy is left unresolved. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html) and Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Petersburg, Hardy County, Va. (now W. Va.)
quote: We marched first to Peters burgh a distance of 30 miles then to Morefield 10 miles then to Strausburgh 55 miles
source_note: Quote: ERM to his sister, Mt. Jackson, 12 June 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Moorefield, Hardy County, Va. (now W. Va.)
source_note: ERM, 12 June 1862: "then to Morefield 10 miles." Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Strasburg, Va. (Strasburg and Staunton Road)
quote: there we engage the enimy & drove them back taking a great many prisoners & one piec of cannon.
source_note: "Strasburg and Staunton Road June 1-2 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM, 12 June 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Mount Jackson, Va.
source_note: "Mt. Jackson June 3 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: New Market, Va.
source_note: "New Market June 4 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Harrisonburg, Va.
source_note: "Harrisonburg June 6 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). ERM: "we followd the retreating rebels as far as Harrisonburgh a distance 47 miles."

place_name: Battle of Cross Keys, Rockingham County, Va.
quote: hearing that then [Ewell] had made a stand 5 miles farther on at a place called Cross Keys we pushed on & attacked them & fought them all day sunday the 8th
source_note: "Battle of Cross Keys June 8 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM to his sister, 12 June 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html). Cross Keys battlefield lies inside the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District but is not a National Park Service unit.

place_name: Port Republic, Va. — pursuit halted at the burned bridge
quote: Monday we drove them back 7 miles where they succedded in crossing the shamadiah at Port republic & burning the brigde which stoped us.
source_note: Quote: ERM to his sister, 12 June 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Mount Jackson, Va.
quote: We are now in a beautiful country the valley of the Shanandoah which is layed wast[e] by the fates of war.
source_note: ERM's letters of 12 and 14 June 1862 are headed Mt. Jackson. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Camp at "Shawsburgh" (place-name not identified; regiment then near Middletown/Strasburg, Va.)
quote: Our regmt now cannot muster over 200 men for a fight 5 captains 2 1st Lieut & 8 2nd Lieut & one field officer which is Major Reily.
source_note: ERM's telegraph-form letter of 21 June 1862 is headed "Camp at Shawsburgh." The name has not been identified; coordinates shown are Middletown, Va., where Dyer's places the regiment through 7 July. Treated as approximate. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html) and Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Middletown, Frederick County, Va.
quote: I have not heard from home for several weeks, but suppose you have been buisy settling up your business & collecting your bills.
source_note: "At Middletown till July 7 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM to his father, Camp near Middletown, 5 July 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Sperryville, Rappahannock County, Va.
quote: we are often called up from our beds to go out and meet our prodigal brothers of C.S.A. who have rebeled against their country & are now reaping the fruits of their sins. Is this not really romantic.
source_note: "and at Sperryville till August 8 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Quote: ERM to his sister, Camp near Sperryville, 27 July 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Madison Court House, Va. — reconnaissance
source_note: "Reconnoissance to Madison Court House July 16-19 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Battle of Cedar Mountain, Culpeper County, Va.
source_note: "Battle of Cedar Mountain August 9 [1862]" is listed in the regiment's service record; McLean's brigade was in the supporting line rather than the main assault, so ERM's personal exposure is not certain. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Cedar Mountain Battlefield is managed by Friends of Cedar Mountain Battlefield / Virginia DCR, not the National Park Service.

place_name: Camp about 12 miles from Culpeper, Va.
quote: It was source of pleasure to me to know that my Commission as 1st Lieut has been made but still I never can be perfectly in this company
source_note: ERM's letters of 17 and 18 Aug. 1862 are headed "In Camp 12 mile from C-" (endorsed "Culpepper"). Exact camp not located; coordinates are Culpeper town. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Freeman's Ford, Rappahannock River, Va.
source_note: "Freeman's Ford August 22 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); see also D. B. Morrow, "In Western Virginia... the 75th Ohio Lost Heavily at Freeman's Ford and Second Bull Run," National Tribune, 14 Aug. 1913.

place_name: Second Battle of Bull Run (Manassas), Va.
source_note: "Battle of Bull Run August 29-30 [1862]." The 75th Ohio lost 113 men and its colors were riddled with ninety balls. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); Whitelaw Reid, Ohio in the War; E. R. Monfort, "The 75th Ohio at Bull Run," National Tribune, 15 March 1917.

place_name: Battle of Chantilly (Ox Hill), Fairfax County, Va.
source_note: Dyer's does not name Chantilly separately for the 75th Ohio; it is covered by "Pope's Campaign in Northern Virginia August 16-September 2, [1862]," which spans the 1 Sept. action at Ox Hill during the army's withdrawal to Fairfax Court House. Confidence marked medium for that reason. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). Today the site is Ox Hill Battlefield Park, a Fairfax County park, not a National Park Service unit.

place_name: Defences of Washington, D.C.
source_note: "Duty in the Defences of Washington, D.C., till December [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html). NOTE: the Wikipedia article on the regiment states that the 75th fought at South Mountain in September 1862; Dyer's, the NPS unit record and Reid's Ohio in the War all place it in the Washington defences at that date, and no South Mountain waypoint is plotted here.

place_name: Bristoe Station and Warrenton Junction, Va. — expedition from Centreville
source_note: "Expedition from Centreville to Bristoe Station and Warrenton Junction September 25-28 [1862]." Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Centreville, Fairfax County, Va.
quote: We are now in the most forlorn & deserted country, I ever saw it is uninhabited & destitute of every thing required to sustain life even of animals
source_note: ERM to his sister, "Army in the field, Centerville Va Oct 8th" [1862], Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Haymarket, Prince William County, Va.
quote: We left Centerville on Sunday Morning camped at Manassas junction & imediately went out to perform Picket duty were much troubled by the Enemies cavelry all night & Proceded to this place via Bull Run Battle field in the Morning
source_note: ERM to his sister, Hay Market, Va., 6 Nov. 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Hopewell Gap, Bull Run Mountains, Va.
quote: We arrived here yesterday from Hopewills Gap a distance of 24 miles in two days march.
source_note: ERM to his father, Chantilly, 21 Nov. 1862, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html). Coordinates for the gap are approximate.

place_name: Chantilly, Fairfax County, Va. — winter camp
quote: we have no stoves & nothing but shelter tents to protect us from the storm. Our tents are full of snow & the cold is almost intolerable being several degrees below zero
source_note: ERM's letters of 21 Nov. and 7 Dec. 1862 are headed Chantilly. Quote from the 7 Dec. letter. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: March to Fredericksburg, Va.
source_note: "March to Fredericksburg, Va., December 10-15 [1862]." The XI Corps was held in reserve and the 75th Ohio was not engaged in the battle. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)
nps_unit: Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park

place_name: Stafford Court House, Va.
quote: We are now at Staffords C.H. 6 miles from Fredricksburgh from which place we have just arrived. We have a very pleasant little Camp in the thickest woods you ever saw of pine & oak.
source_note: ERM's letters of 19 Dec. (headed "/61" but unmistakably 1862 from its content) and 9 Jan. 1863 are headed Stafford Court House. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: The "Mud March," Stafford County, Va.
source_note: "'Mud March' January 20-24, 1863." Coordinates approximate the route up the north bank of the Rappahannock toward Banks' Ford. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Belle Plain landing, Stafford County, Va.
quote: Mud versus Snow. Just as the little branches peep out from under the snow, the mules & boys peep out from under the mud, as if afraid to venture far, & some times nothing is visable save the tips of their ears.
source_note: ERM's letters of 24 Jan. and 2 Feb. 1863 are headed Bell Plain(s). Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Brooke Station, Stafford County, Va.
quote: Lieut Genl Hooker has assumed command of the army of the potomac we have had to submit to the most minute inspections of all Company property
source_note: "At Falmouth till April 27 [1863]" (Dyer's); ERM wrote on 2 Feb. "We march to morrow to Brooks Station" and his 25 Feb. letter is headed Brooks Station. Sources: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html) and Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Kelly's Ford and Germanna Ford, Rappahannock and Rapidan Rivers, Va. — Chancellorsville flank march
quote: we left camp at 4 A.M. on Monday Apr 26. marched three days 60 miles around in the rear of Fredericksburgh
source_note: "Chancellorsville Campaign April 27-May 6 [1863]" (Dyer's). ERM dates the start 26 April; Dyer's says 27 April. Coordinates are Kelly's Ford, the XI Corps' Rappahannock crossing. Sources: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html) and Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Battle of Chancellorsville, Spotsylvania County, Va.
quote: where occurred one of the most desparate fights of the war where in 15 minutes we lost 6 commissioned officers Col Reily wound & prisoner Adjt Gano missing Capt Morey & Capt Watkins wounded & in the hands of the Enimy
source_note: "Battle of Chancellorsville May 1-5 [1863]." The 75th Ohio, in Ames'/McLean's brigade of the XI Corps, stood and fired for about ten minutes against Jackson's flank attack on 2 May; Col. Robert Reily was killed and about 150 of the regiment were killed or wounded. Sources: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); Wikipedia, "75th Ohio Infantry Regiment"; E. R. Monfort, "The First Division, Eleventh Corps, at Chancellorsville" (G.A.R. War Papers, 1891). Quote: ERM to his sister, 8 May 1863, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)
nps_unit: Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park

place_name: Camp near Brooke Station / Stafford County, Va. — after Chancellorsville
quote: the old 75th looks thin Genl McLean shed tears yesterday speaking to the regt
source_note: ERM's 8 May 1863 letter is headed only "Hd Qts 75th Regt OVI"; the XI Corps returned to its Stafford County camps after the battle, so the location is inferred. Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Gettysburg Campaign — XI Corps march north through Catlett's Station and Centreville, Va.
source_note: "Gettysburg (Pa.) Campaign June 11-July 24 [1863]." Dyer's gives no intermediate stops for the regiment; the coordinates follow the XI Corps' documented route north through Centreville and are approximate. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html)

place_name: Middletown, Frederick County, Maryland
source_note: XI Corps route of march into Maryland during the Gettysburg Campaign; not itemised in the regiment's service record, so marked medium. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html) (campaign dates) plus standard XI Corps itineraries.

place_name: Emmitsburg, Frederick County, Maryland
source_note: The XI Corps camped at and around Emmitsburg on 30 June 1863 and marched from there to Gettysburg on the morning of 1 July. Source: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html) (campaign) and standard Gettysburg Campaign itineraries.

place_name: Barlow's Knoll (Blocher's Knoll), north of Gettysburg, Pa.
source_note: The 75th Ohio arrived with the XI Corps mid-day 1 July 1863 and took position on Blocher's Knoll in Barlow's division; the salient was overwhelmed by Doles' and Gordon's brigades and the regiment withdrew through the town to Cemetery Hill. Sources: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); Wikipedia, "75th Ohio Infantry Regiment"; monuments of the 25th & 75th Ohio on East Howard Avenue.

place_name: East Cemetery Hill (the brickyard lane), Gettysburg, Pa.
source_note: On the evening of 2 July 1863 the 75th Ohio, between the 25th Ohio and 17th Connecticut on the brickyard lane at the base of East Cemetery Hill, helped repulse Hays' Louisiana brigade. The regiment lost 186 officers and men at Gettysburg (16 killed, 74 wounded, 96 missing). Sources: Dyer's Compendium / NPS Battle Unit record, 75th Regiment, Ohio Infantry (nps.gov/civilwar UOH0075RI; ohiocivilwar.com/cw75.html); Busey & Martin, Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg; the 25th/75th Ohio monument on Wainwright Avenue.

place_name: Gettysburg battlefield / Gettysburg National Military Park — ERM severely wounded
quote: Elias wounded severely Come immediately
source_note: ERM was severely wounded in the hip/thigh on 2 July 1863; the bullet carried fragments of his own sword into the wound. Quote: telegram, J. W. Monfort (U.S. Sanitary Commission) to Rev. J. G. Monfort, sent from Gettysburg 9 July 1863, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html). Biography supplied by the family.

place_name: Gettysburg, Pa. — recovering at the home of his cousin Sarah (Thompson) Monfort
quote: My wife has been out here two weeks and we have been stopping at our old home, Mrs. Thompson's, I did not think, at the time you left, that I should remain in old Gettysburg so long
source_note: ERM was nursed after his wounding at the home of his cousin Sarah (Thompson) Monfort in Gettysburg (family account; see also Sarah Monfort's letter of 19 July 1863 held by the family). The quote is from G. A. Evans to Capt. Monfort, Gettysburg, 9 Oct. 1863, Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html), written from "Mrs. Thompson's." The exact house has not been located, so the coordinates are the town centre and confidence is medium.

place_name: The Lightner Farmhouse, 2350 Baltimore Pike, Gettysburg, Pa.
quote: I have been with Elias this day - he is better, did not think he would live for a day or two past. Have telegraphed but no word from you. He is at the house of Mr. Lightner on Baltimore Pike, 4 miles from Gettysburgh. I look for you ther - he is not with his corps.
source_note: Confirmed by a letter from Isaac Watts Monfort to his brother, Rev. Joseph Glass Monfort, dated 11 July 1863 from Gettysburg: "He is at the house of Mr. Lightner on Baltimore Pike 4 miles from Gettysburgh." Also corroborated by the Lightner Farmhouse Bed & Breakfast's own history (a guest room is named for ERM): https://www.lightnerfarmhouse.com/monfort-photos . Address confirmed via Adams County, PA property records (APN 30-G15-0014-000, Mount Joy Township). Original document: iwm_to_jgm_18630711_gettysburg_letter.jpg (Supporting Documents and Files), verified 2026-08-04.

place_name: Glendale, Ohio — convalescent at home
quote: My idea is that you can be brought home on a good bed without danger. If when you get to Pittsburgh you find you are not able to go by rail, you can take a boat for Cincinnati.
source_note: ERM's father wrote on 12 Aug. 1863 planning to bring him home; by 21 Oct. 1863 his cousin Edward Riggs wrote "I heard that you had arrived at home." Source: Hanover College Monfort letters transcript (history.hanover.edu/texts/HC/Monfort-all.html)

place_name: Glendale, Ohio — discharged for disability from his Gettysburg wound
source_note: ERM discharged 9 December 1863 on account of the wound received at Gettysburg. Source: family biography; Official Roster of the Soldiers of the State of Ohio, vol. 6 (75th O.V.I.).

place_name: Hanover College, Hanover, Indiana
source_note: Coda, beyond the military path: ERM returned to Hanover College in 1864 and graduated in 1865. Month is nominal (start of the academic year); only the year is documented. Source: family biography; the Elias Riggs Monfort Collection is held at Hanover College's Duggan Library.
